question: Do temporal fraction observations localise the common mass-transfer-rate multiplier more strongly than cumulative cup observations, on the same shots and the same model?
same_campaign_caveat: The model parameters were originally fitted in this source lineage. This is a same-campaign observation-operator study, NOT independent physical validation.

arm_definitions.CUP_CURVE_3: three cumulative cup concentrations, brew ratios 1/1, 1/2, 1/3
arm_definitions.CUP_FINAL_1: final cumulative cup concentration only, brew ratio 1/3

negative_control.claim: the rate profile is exactly flat for every kappa
negative_control.proof: one observation y and one free level I give the exact MAPE minimiser I* = y/f(kappa); then |I* f(kappa) - y| = 0 identically, so the per-shot MAPE is 0 at every kappa and the profile is constant
negative_control.status: analytic; verified numerically in the results
negative_control.consequence: carries no rate information and is not counted as evidence for any arm

grind_policy.primary: shots at GL 1.7 only; declared grain parameters match the actual grind
grind_policy.sensitivity: all admitted shots under the port's documented centre-grind approximation (solver.py: psi/d_s2 vary <15% across grinds, effect on MAPE second order)
grind_policy.why: the per-experiment grind assignment is opaque in the source, so no declared parameter set exists for GL 1.4 or GL 2.0. Using GL 1.7 parameters for those shots is an approximation, not a measurement, and is reported as a sensitivity rather than as the primary result.

objectives.primary: shot-balanced MAPE with exact per-shot level profiling
objectives.weighting: shots weighted equally, so six fraction rows do not give a shot six times the influence of a three-point cup curve

positivity.rule: every prediction and observation strictly positive (protocol 1.1)
positivity.why: at high kappa the bed is exhausted before the late fractions, so late interval-average predictions reach zero and then go slightly negative. Those kappa are EXCLUDED and recorded, never clipped.
